title: [FND-01] Run a minimal Blender document lifecycle and undo experiment
body:
## Goal
Collect reproducible evidence for the first Blender compatibility baseline. B-CAD is currently a blueprint; this issue is a small host-integration experiment, not a supported add-on release.

Roadmap: **FND-01**, informing **CORE-06**. Read the [architecture proposal](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) and [research register](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/docs/research.md).

## Bounded deliverables
- Propose a small set of candidate Blender builds using primary release/support documentation. Record exact build, OS, CPU architecture, and Python version for every result.
- Build a disposable, dependency-free experiment that stores a UUID, schema version, and integer revision as document data. Exercise register/unregister, edit, cancel, undo, redo, save, close, reopen, and two simultaneous Blender instances.
- Supply clean-checkout reproduction instructions, observed results, API assumptions, and a short recommendation with unresolved questions. Use an original test scene.

## Acceptance criteria
A reviewer can reproduce the lifecycle on at least one named build; the restored revision is observable after undo/redo and reopen; unsupported or untested combinations are marked explicitly. The report compares observations with current primary documentation and does not declare support for untested platforms. A maintainer reviews the proposed baseline in an ADR before it becomes a compatibility promise.

Follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md); major workflow decisions need a Design RFC. Disclose all AI assistance under the [AI policy](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/docs/ai-contributions.md), including the actual model/version and accountable contributor.

title: [FND-02] Create a pinned dependency and redistribution research matrix
body:
## Goal
Make dependency choices reviewable before any CAD binaries are bundled. This is a provenance inventory for a blueprint-stage project; it does not approve dependencies or give legal conclusions.

Roadmap: **FND-02**. Start with the open questions in [research.md](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/docs/research.md) and the boundaries in [ADR 0001](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/docs/decisions/0001-cad-architecture.md).

## Bounded deliverables
Create one research document covering OCCT, SolveSpace/libslvs, and the proposed PlaneGCS extraction only. For each candidate record a source URL and exact tag/commit, component/license-file paths, build requirements, immediate dependencies, packaging assumptions, attribution/notice information, and questions needing further review. Clearly distinguish source-file SPDX declarations from conclusions about the full distribution.

Check the current official requirements for the project's own GitHub Releases route and any proposed Blender extension channel. Link dated primary sources and flag inaccessible or ambiguous policies. Do not copy third-party source or full license documents merely to populate the matrix.

## Acceptance criteria
Every factual row has a primary source and source pin; unknowns remain explicit; required follow-up work has a named decision rather than an inferred approval. The report proposes the smallest dependency scope for FND-03/FND-04 and requests maintainer review before integration.

Use the [contributor workflow](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [AI disclosure policy](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/docs/ai-contributions.md). A repository license choice alone does not authorize third-party redistribution.

title: [FND-03] Prototype one isolated OCCT solid, measurement, and STEP round trip
body:
## Goal
Test the proposed native-core boundary with one small, independently checkable part. No Blender integration or production feature engine is required for this experiment.

Roadmap: **FND-03**; prerequisite: relevant **FND-02** dependency review. Read [ADR 0001](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/docs/decisions/0001-cad-architecture.md) and the [architecture proposal](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/docs/architecture.md). Open or link the required Design RFC before introducing the dependency/build choice.

## Bounded deliverables
- Pin a reviewed OCCT source version and provide a clean native build on one named OS/CPU/compiler combination.
- Construct an original 40 × 20 × 5 mm box with one radius-3 mm cylindrical through-hole, entirely outside Blender.
- Validate the solid, query bounds and volume, generate tessellation, export STEP, and re-import it into a fresh evaluation context.
- Publish reproduction commands, build/source provenance, measured results, documented tolerance, and known failures.

## Acceptance criteria
A reviewer can repeat the experiment from a clean checkout. Body count and validity survive round trip; dimensions and volume agree with the declared tolerance and analytic expectation of **4000 − 45π mm³**. Tessellation is finite and labeled as display/export approximation. The experiment does not create a supported package or select a permanent kernel version by itself.

Follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [AI policy](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/docs/ai-contributions.md): disclose model/version, authored scope, exact checks, and accountable contributor; AI-authored code/architecture must satisfy the owner's stated capability requirement and receive human review.

title: [FND-04] Compare solver diagnostics on a single constrained rectangle
body:
## Goal
Produce one small, fair slice of the sketch-solver comparison instead of attempting a full sketcher. The result informs the larger **FND-04** bake-off and does not select a winning backend.

Prerequisite: relevant **FND-02** dependency review. Read the [solver boundary](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) and [research contribution guidance](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/docs/research.md).

## Bounded deliverables
Define the same four-line rectangle in solver-independent terms: coincident corners, horizontal/vertical edges, width, height, and optional origin anchor. Compare pinned SolveSpace/libslvs and PlaneGCS versions on four cases: free translation, fully constrained, redundant dimension, and conflicting dimensions. Record residuals/status, available degrees-of-freedom/conflict diagnostics, repeatability, and translation effort. If a backend cannot be extracted or built within scope, document the blocking evidence and a minimal next experiment.

Include tiny original fixtures, exact environment/commands, and primary API references. Use a Design RFC before adding dependencies or permanent interfaces. Keep timing exploratory and identify hardware; one rectangle is not a general performance benchmark.

## Acceptance criteria
A reviewer can reproduce at least one backend and inspect a precise equivalent mapping for the other. The report distinguishes unsupported diagnostics from missing implementation, preserves identical intended constraint semantics, records failures, and recommends the next comparison without freezing the document format.

Follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [AI contribution policy](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/docs/ai-contributions.md). Disclose models, assistance scope, provenance, unrun checks, and human review status.

title: [FND-07] Specify six topology-reference edit cases before building a resolver
body:
## Goal
Define observable reference intent for a small regression corpus. This is an original, implementation-independent fixture specification for **FND-07**, informing **SOL-03**. We do not have a persistent-reference implementation yet.

Read [persistent topology references](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) and the [reference questions](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/docs/research.md).

## Bounded deliverables
Describe exactly six small cases: extrusion length change after a fillet; source-edge split; coplanar-face merge; hole relocation changing adjacency; upstream suppression/restoration; pattern count **4 → 7 → 3**. For each provide dimensions/units, construction steps, the selected semantic source, downstream operation, upstream edit, expected preserved reference or explicitly unresolved outcome, and independent geometry checks. Include at least one intentionally ambiguous case where asking for repair is the correct result.

Original diagrams or hand-authored parameter tables are welcome. Record authorship and permission to redistribute every fixture; avoid customer/proprietary CAD files. No kernel build is necessary to submit the specification.

## Acceptance criteria
A geometry reviewer can reconstruct each case without guessing the selected face/edge or expected intent. Every case distinguishes a correct result, a visible failure, and a dangerous silent retarget. The corpus does not rely on face indices, screenshots alone, or a claim that arbitrary topology changes must be lossless.

Use the [contributor guide](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [AI policy](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/docs/ai-contributions.md). AI materially determining architectural expectations must meet the stated capability requirement and receive human review.

title: [SK-06] Describe a beginner's first measured-bracket workflow
body:
## Goal
Help us design a first-part experience before there is an add-on to install. This newcomer-friendly task needs clear observation and plain language, not CAD-kernel programming. It informs **SK-06** and **REL-05**.

Start with [the roadmap](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/ROADMAP.md) and the [glossary](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/docs/glossary.md).

## Bounded deliverables
Write one proposed user story for an original simple bracket: create a millimeter document, sketch a dimensioned rectangle, name a thickness parameter, extrude, make a through-hole, change one dimension, inspect a measurement, save/reopen, and export. Supply a small dimension table and explain the visible feedback or question the user expects at each step. Identify the three most confusing terms/actions and suggest plain-language wording.

Use text or original wireframes clearly labeled **proposed workflow / mockup**. Tell us whether the story comes from your own modeling experience, an observed user session, or desk research. Do not claim usability testing that did not happen.

## Acceptance criteria
A reader unfamiliar with B-CAD can follow the intended sequence and explain the intended resulting part. The proposal identifies units, design intent, editability, and recovery expectations. It links unavailable capabilities to roadmap IDs and never reads as installation instructions for existing software. Major workflow adoption remains subject to a Design RFC.

Follow [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and disclose any assistance using the [AI policy](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/docs/ai-contributions.md). Human contributions without AI are fully welcome.

title: [SK-06] Propose a keyboard-first sketch and constraint feedback checklist
body:
## Goal
Make accessibility part of the future sketch interaction design. This is a bounded checklist/proposal for **SK-06** and **REL-05**, suitable for contributors who use keyboard navigation, high contrast, magnification, or other accessibility workflows. No Blender or native build is required.

Read the [proposed sketch boundary](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/docs/architecture.md) and [contribution guidance](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Bounded deliverables
Take five proposed actions: enter a dimension, inspect remaining degrees of freedom, locate a conflicting constraint, repair a broken reference, and cancel a preview. For each specify a keyboard path, focus/selection feedback, concise status text, and a non-color signal. List questions that require testing in the eventual Blender integration. Include one original annotated wireframe or a plain-text interaction table.

If you gather feedback, document the method, consent, and limitations without publishing personal information. First-person accessibility experience is useful evidence; a checklist alone is not a certification. This issue targets future add-on interaction, not another general website polish pass.

## Acceptance criteria
All five actions have observable success, failure, and cancel states. No status depends solely on color, hover, or a precise mouse gesture. Proposals distinguish host constraints needing verification from implemented support, and major workflow choices are offered for Design RFC review.

Complete [AI disclosure](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/docs/ai-contributions.md) when applicable. Do not claim screen-reader compatibility, conformance, or tested users without evidence.

title: Propose a one-language translation pilot with an update policy
body:
## Goal
Help non-English contributors join without creating an unmaintainable translation tree. This is a planning contribution for one language you can review fluently; it is not a request to machine-translate the whole repository.

Start with [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md), the [glossary](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/docs/glossary.md), and the [installation status](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/docs/installation.md). It supports the roadmap's newcomer learning path in **REL-05**.

## Bounded deliverables
Propose a pilot for one language with: intended readers; a short list of first pages; a 10-term CAD glossary including sketch, constraint, feature, body, occurrence, and tolerance; a translated sample of no more than two introductory paragraphs; a reviewer/update process; and a way to show when a translation's English source has changed. Suggest file/navigation conventions for review before creating new infrastructure.

## Acceptance criteria
A fluent reviewer can check the sample, the blueprint-stage warning remains accurate, links and technical identifiers remain usable, and the plan names who can review future updates or explicitly asks for a volunteer. Terminology choices explain ambiguous words. The proposal preserves source attribution and makes no promise of a supported localized add-on.

Use the [AI policy](https://github.com/Ramses13th/B-CAD/blob/main/docs/ai-contributions.md) to disclose translation assistance and model/version. Mark human language review as pending if it has not happened. You do not need to use AI to contribute.
